## Summary

Fixes #37100.

The DEV-only Performance Tracks instrumentation added in 19.2.0 reads `window.event` unconditionally in `trackSchedulerEvent()`, `resolveEventType()`, and `resolveEventTimeStamp()`. `trackSchedulerEvent()` runs at the entry of Scheduler-driven tasks (`performWorkOnRootViaSchedulerTask`, `processRootScheduleInImmediateTask`, and the passive-effects flush scheduled by `commitRoot`). These tasks live on deferred `setImmediate` ticks and can legitimately fire after a per-test-file DOM environment (jsdom / happy-dom under vitest or jest) has been torn down. When that happens the task throws `ReferenceError: window is not defined` before doing any work, which fails entire CI suites with an unhandled error attributed to the next, innocent test file.

This guards the three reads with `typeof window !== 'undefined'`, matching the bundle's existing convention for `window` accesses that may run outside a browser DOM (e.g. `canUseDOM`, the `window.ErrorEvent` detection in the error-reporting path). When `window` is gone the attribution resolves to `undefined`, i.e. "no event", which is accurate. `shouldAttemptEagerTransition()` and `resolveUpdatePriority()` are left untouched: they only run while an update is being dispatched, so `window` is alive by construction there.

## How did you test this change?

- Added a regression test (`ReactDOMWindowTeardown-test.js`, node environment + manually constructed JSDOM mirroring the issue's repro). It fails on `main` with `ReferenceError: window is not defined` from `performWorkOnRootViaSchedulerTask` and passes with this change.
- `yarn test ReactPerformanceTrack ReactDOMFiberAsync ReactDOMNativeEventHeuristic` — all pass.
- `yarn linc`, `yarn flow dom-node`, `yarn prettier` — clean.
- Ran the repro script from #37100 verbatim: against published `react-dom@19.2.8` it crashes as reported; against a locally built `NODE_DEV` bundle with this change it prints `done, no crash` and exits 0.
